questions: Do you find that your eyelids droop more towards the end of the day or after you have been reading or looking at screens?
Do you experience double vision that comes and goes?
Do you have any difficulty chewing food, swallowing, or holding your head up when you are tired?
Does your vision or eyelid position improve after you take a nap?
Have you had this droopy eyelid since you were a baby, or did it develop later in life?
Is it only one eye that is affected, or are both eyes involved?
Have you ever been told you have a thyroid problem or been tested for thyroid issues?
Do you have any eye pain, grittiness, or pressure behind your eyes?
Has anyone ever commented that your eyes look "staring" or that you look surprised?
Have you ever noticed that your eyelids look different from other family members, such as your parents or siblings?
When you look at the video frames, does what you see match how your eyes normally look?
Do you have any eyelid twitching or involuntary movements of your eyelids?
Did you notice anything different about your eyelids in photos or videos of yourself before this one?
Do you have any difficulty with your peripheral vision or is your vision completely normal?
Are you concerned about the appearance of your eyes, or is there a functional problem you are experiencing?
Have you had your vision tested recently, and if so, were there any issues with your eyesight in either eye?
When you try to open your eyes wide, can you lift your eyelids much higher than what we see in these frames?
Looking at childhood photos of yourself, did your eyelids appear to sit lower than other children's?
Did your parents or teachers ever mention that you held your head in a particular way to see?
Is the droopiness the same on both sides, or do you notice one side is slightly worse?
Have you ever had any surgeries or procedures on your eyes or eyelids?
Do you take any medications regularly, including over-the-counter supplements?
Have you ever been evaluated by an eye specialist (ophthalmologist) before for your eyelids?
Do you have to tilt your head backward to see properly when walking or reading?
Have your parents or relatives ever mentioned that you had "sleepy looking eyes" as a child?
Have you noticed any asymmetry between your eyes or do they look the same to you?
orders: Measurement of levator muscle function (margin reflex distance and levator excursion)
Assessment of frontalis muscle use (checking if forehead wrinkles are present when trying to look up)
Phenylephrine drop test - apply phenylephrine eye drops and observe if ptosis improves
Pupil examination - check if pupils are equal and reactive to light
